channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Delaware dog custody battle wraps up with unexpected auction
item.description: Delaware's Chancery Court ended a lengthy custody battle over a goldendoodle named Tucker by ordering a sealed bid auction between the estranged owners.

item.title: Footnote in legal-mal case spawns debate over tolling
item.description: Massachusetts judge dismisses legal malpractice suit as untimely, ruling adverse court decisions put clients on notice of harm despite ongoing litigation.

item.title: Securities – Standing
item.description: Where claims of conversion, breach of fiduciary duty, negligence and violation of the Uniform Securities Act (G.L.c. 110A) were dismissed for lack of subject matter jurisdiction, the judgment of dismissal must be vacated because the plaintiffs' allegations of injury suffice to establish standing.

item.title: Products liability – Preemption – Medical device
item.description: Where a plaintiff has brought a product liability action asserting personal injury claims against the designers, manufacturers and sellers of a medical device that failed during her hysterectomy surgery, a motion to dismiss should be denied because the plaintiff’s claims are not preempted despite the defendants’ contention that only the FDA can enforce violations of the Food and Drug Cosmetic Act.

item.title: Employment – Referral bonus – Wage Act
item.description: Where two plaintiffs have brought a putative class action alleging that their former employer withheld payments that they had earned through its employee referral program, their claim under the Massachusetts Wage Act must be dismissed because the referral bonus payments at issue are not “wages” under the statute, but they have plausibly alleged a claim for breach of contract.

item.title: Testator can serve as witness to joint codicil with spouse
item.description: A Massachusetts Probate &amp;amp;amp; Family Court judge ruled a testator may serve as a witness to a jointly executed codicil, emphasizing testamentary intent over formalities.

item.title: Constitutional – Unclaimed property – Interest
item.description: Where a plaintiff brought a putative class action alleging that the interest-payment provisions in the Massachusetts Disposition of Unclaimed Property Act have resulted in an uncompensated taking of his private property for public use, the dismissal of his complaint should be upheld because (1) his challenge to the interest rate under the statute is not ripe and (2) he lacks standing to seek injunctive or declaratory relief.

item.title: Immigration – Motion to reopen sua sponte
item.description: Where the Board of Immigration Appeals denied a motion to reopen sua sponte, that decision should be upheld because the two petitioners have not identified any legal or constitutional error in the board’s determination that they did not present an “exceptional situation” that warranted reopening.

item.title: Criminal – Conspiracy – Hearsay
item.description: Where three defendants were convicted of conspiracy to violate the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act and conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute a controlled substance, the convictions should be affirmed despite their contention that certain statements were wrongly admitted into evidence at their joint trial.

item.title: Employment – Trade secrets
item.description: Where a jury verdict in favor of a plaintiff was set aside with respect to the plaintiff’s trade secret claims, the trial judge’s decision should be affirmed because the plaintiff has failed to establish that any financial information or “internal strategy” qualifies as a trade secret under Massachusetts law and the Defend Trade Secrets Act.

item.title: Education – Special education – ‘Place’ regulation
item.description: Where plaintiff parents have challenged a Massachusetts regulation requiring that special education services funded with state or local funds be provided in a public school facility or other public or neutral site, the dismissal of the plaintiffs’ complaint should be affirmed because (1) the plaintiffs fail to plausibly allege that the regulation infringes on their fundamental parental right to direct the education of their children and (2) the regulation otherwise survives rational basis review

item.title: Suffolk DA: Law expanding CPCS hiring tilting pay landscape
item.description: Suffolk County District Attorney Kevin Hayden applauded the Legislature on March 24 for the law it passed last summer to end a work stoppage among some bar advocates. But he said that law also spun off "some, I think, unintended consequences that simply have to be addressed."

item.title: Judge dismisses $5M lawsuit over fatal shooting by Milford officer
item.description: A federal judge has dismissed a $5 million civil complaint filed by the mother of a man who was fatally shot nearly six years ago by a Milford police officer.

item.title: Trump administration to pay $1B to stop two East Coast wind farms
item.description: The Trump administration agreed to pay $1 billion to TotalEnergies to stop two offshore wind farms off New York and North Carolina, redirecting funds to oil and gas projects.

item.title: Consumer protection – TCPA – Private right of action
item.description: Where a plaintiff has filed a complaint under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act alleging a violation of 47 C.F.R. §64.1601(e)(1) by failing to transmit caller ID information, the defendant’s motion to dismiss should be denied because the plaintiff has a private right of action to enforce that regulation.
